newsitem.title: GERMANY: German 1996 growth driven by exports - stats office.
newsitem.headline: German 1996 growth driven by exports - stats office.

text.p: German economic growth in 1996 was driven mainly by exports, capital investment and state spending, the Federal Statistics Office said on Thursday.

"The demand side of GDP shows that in 1996 export demand, demand for capital goods and state consumption made an above-average contribution to economic growth," Statistics Office President Johann Hahlen told a news conference.
The statistics office also said the economy would remain weak in 1997, but that conditions would be favourable.
